# App 2 preregistration — file-manager-basic

Schema `mssp.product-preregistration/v0` · revision `v0` · position `02`

> CANDIDATE PREREGISTRATION. It defines what later work must prove; it does not authorize product code, provider calls, merge, release or deployment.

## Product boundary

A root-scoped Windows workspace file manager lets a user select one real directory, inspect and navigate its contents, refresh external changes, select one or more entries, create a directory, rename, copy, move and send files or directories to the Windows Recycle Bin. It does not claim to replace Explorer.

One selected root is always visible; changing it is explicit; navigation above it is refused. Remembered-root persistence is not required.

## Primary GUI workflow

1. **W01** — launch the packaged application
1. **W02** — choose the pinned acceptance root and render its first exact directory snapshot
1. **W03** — navigate into the pinned child directory and back to the selected root
1. **W04** — perform an external create and remove, then refresh and render the new exact snapshot
1. **W05** — select one entry, then select multiple entries by snapshot-scoped opaque entry IDs
1. **W06** — create one directory with a single-segment name
1. **W07** — rename one regular file without silent overwrite
1. **W08** — copy one binary file and one directory tree within the selected root
1. **W09** — move one regular file and one directory tree within the selected root
1. **W10** — run one multi-entry mutation in which at least one entry succeeds and one controlled entry fails, and render partial per-entry outcomes
1. **W11** — send one disposable file and one disposable directory tree to the Windows Recycle Bin without exposing permanent delete
1. **W12** — close and relaunch the application, explicitly select the same root again, and render a fresh snapshot
1. **W13** — an independent tree-and-byte oracle verifies every expected path, absence, payload and directory boundary

## Result and snapshot contract

Overall: `accepted | partial | refused | failed`.
Per entry: `accepted | refused | failed`.

Generation has one meaning only: it identifies the published snapshot sequence. Every published snapshot increments it exactly once, whether publication follows refresh or mutation. Mutation truth comes from per-entry outcomes.

Snapshot result states: `current | unchanged | unavailable`. The unavailable arm carries no fabricated snapshot and requires a typed observation code.

## V0 reparse and path boundary

Reparse entries may be displayed, but a reparse root, traversal through a reparse entry and mutation through one are refused. Resolved-string containment is not claimed as race-safe confinement.

## Deferred and excluded

- **Deferred `open-with-default-application`:** Electron and the Windows default-application route do not promise a new child PID and may reuse an existing process. A test helper would measure a different operation.
- Excluded: empty-file creation

- Excluded: cross-device move

## Fixtures and action shape

13 pinned directories, 17 pinned files, 205 payload bytes. Payload hex and SHA-256 are owned by independent acceptance, not derived by the product.

Every dynamic subject must prove its precondition before action. An unproved precondition is `DID_NOT_APPLY` and an acceptance failure; it never counts as a caught attack.

- `copy-directory-tree`: one_gui_batch_command; subject copy-dir exact manifest subtree; stop when overall result and snapshot state are rendered.
- `move-directory-tree`: one_gui_batch_command; subject move-dir exact manifest subtree; stop when overall result and snapshot state are rendered.

The caps are hang detectors, not performance claims. Replacing a GUI batch command with a test-side loop changes the subject and fails acceptance.

Every cap breach is classified as `product_hang`, `instrument_subject_mismatch` or `environment_limit`. Only a proven product hang fails the product; harness mismatch invalidates the harness and environment limits remain `NotMeasured`.
